subject: USCIS form editions and filing fees
why_this_lane_and_not_a_wider_one: docs/EXTERNAL-AUTHORITY-PLAN.md, Rank 4: 'Pick one narrow lane and hold it --
immigration form and fee changes is the strongest candidate.'
A changelog across five agencies is a worse asset than a changelog across one,
for a reason that is structural rather than editorial. The thing a journalist
cites is 'the record that has watched this page every week since 2026'. That
record is only worth citing if it is unbroken. Every additional agency adds
another page that can move its URL, another fetch that can fail, and another
week where the changelog is partially blind while still publishing. Depth is
the product; breadth is the thing that destroys it.
USCIS form and fee changes were chosen over the alternatives because:
- they change on a real cadence (edition dates, fee rules) rather than never;
- the primary source is a stable federal URL, not a state board PDF that
- Professional Resource Library already carries the immigration surface
(uscis-medical-exam-resources.html and its cost page), so the changelog
lands next to material it actually relates to;
- the affected reader is specific and currently unserved: someone mid-filing
who needs to know whether the edition they downloaded is still accepted.
boundary: This lane reports WHAT CHANGED on a government page and WHEN it was observed.
It does not tell anyone what to do about it, which edition to file, or whether
they qualify for anything. That boundary is the publication's, not this file's:
data/publications.json 'professional' says the publication is educational only
and does not provide professional advice.

_why_multiple_agents: Tried in order. A self-identifying agent is the courteous default and it is
what a laptop gets 200 with. It is NOT what uscis.gov serves to a datacenter
address: on 2026-09-02 all three pages returned HTTP 403 to a GitHub Actions
runner and 200 to the same request from a laptop, so the block is on the
caller rather than on the page. The browser agent is tried first from CI for
that reason, and which one worked is recorded in state.json.

_reachability_finding_2026_09_02: www.uscis.gov returns HTTP 403 Forbidden to a GitHub Actions runner, for all
three tracked pages, with every one of three declared user agents. The
identical request returns 200 from a laptop. Confirmed twice, on runs
33575030786 and 33575235414. It is an edge bot rule keyed on the caller, not
a missing page and not an outage.
The guard behaved correctly throughout -- nothing was published as 'no
change', no snapshot advanced, and every source named its stop. But a lane
that names a stop every week forever is still a lane that observes nothing,
which is the other half of Rule 0.
So the SPINE of this changelog is now the Federal Register API, which is:
- a United States government primary source (Office of the Federal
Register / GPO), not an intermediary or a scraper proxy;
- built for programmatic access, with no bot rule -- verified 200 from CI;
- a BETTER change record for this subject, because a Federal Register
document IS a dated change with an official citation number, rather than
a webpage state that has to be diffed to find out when it moved.
The three uscis.gov pages stay declared and are still attempted, marked
best_effort. Their 403 is a NAMED, DISCLOSED stop that never turns the
workflow red and is printed on the published page, because a reader must be
able to see which sources are actually being observed. They resolve on their
own the day the block lifts or the lane runs from anywhere else.
